basis: Bilateral congenital absence or hypoplasia of the humeri is a skeletal limb reduction defect.
Metaplastic lesion located in the urethral urothelium; the urethra belongs to the renal axis.
In situ germ cell carcinoma confined to testicular seminiferous tubules; reproductive tumour without defined endocrine dysfunction.
Pulmonary lymphatic malformation defines disease; heart failure and chylopericardium are frequent (30-79%), supporting cardiac involvement.
Neoplasm arising in the common bile duct; extrahepatic bile ducts belong to the hepatic axis.
CNS, ear and cardiac malformations define embryopathy; cleft palate occurs in 30-79%. Nail hypoplasia (30-79%) omitted by cap.
Congenital abnormal drainage of pulmonary veins is a vascular/cardiac defect; respiratory symptoms do not establish lung damage.
Congenital structural abnormality of the inferior vena cava.
Craniosynostosis and ocular/eyelid malformations characterize syndrome; frequencies of developmental and cardiac impairment are unspecified.
Obstetric displacement of the uterus; associated acute hemorrhage does not itself establish a blood or coagulation disorder.
Inherited VWF-related coagulation and platelet dysfunction; bleeding symptoms do not establish organ damage. Angiodysplasia is a separately diagnosed vascular lesion.
Inherited bile acid synthesis disorder with defining hepatic fibrosis and failure; iron deficiency anemia is a separate condition.
Benign adipose tissue neoplasm arising in renal parenchyma or the renal capsule.
Mosaic NF1 produces localized peripheral nerve sheath tumours and characteristic skin lesions; other organ damage is not common across presentations.
Myeloid malignancy affecting marrow and blood; recurrent infections are complications, and extramedullary damage lacks a qualifying frequency.
Inherited skin disorder defined by hyperpigmentation and palmoplantar hyperkeratosis.
Neurodevelopmental impairment defines syndrome; strabismus occurs in 4/4 assessed, supporting ocular dysfunction, although esotropia is reported in only 4/18 overall.
Demyelinating peripheral neuropathy; persistent muscle atrophy occurs in 80-99%, distal amyotrophy in 8/8 and pes cavus in 9/9.
Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disorder causing optic nerve degeneration; nonoptic neuropathy, myopathy and arrhythmia occur in 5-29%.
Neurodegeneration, retinal dystrophy and hearing loss define syndrome; fixed limb contractures occur in 1/1 assessed and cubitus valgus in 2/2.
Skeletal dysplasia affecting bone epiphyses and metaphyses.
Mature B-cell lymphoma warrants blood-cell and lymphoma mechanism axes; no particular extranodal organ is affected commonly enough across the group.
Malignant retinal tumour involving one eye.
Inherited retinal dystrophy defined by retinal degeneration; neurological ancestry does not establish extraocular neurological damage.
Cryptophthalmos 2/3, renal agenesis 2/3 and syndactyly define syndrome; tracheal atresia/lung anomaly reported in 1/3. Hydrocephalus 1/3 omitted by cap.
